title: Usage Limit Handoff
eyebrow: Design for approval · save and hand off work at 90% of a usage limit · nothing built yet

short.lead: When a session reaches 90% of its five-hour or weekly usage limit, it should stop starting new work, write a handoff note, commit and push everything to its branch, and give you one line to paste into a session on your other Claude account. This replaces open issue #140 ("auto create a handoff document at 95% usage and commit all current changes"), and answers its two open questions: the percentage is the plan's usage limit, not the context window, and the note goes in docs/5-today/. The catch is detection. No hook can read your usage percentage. The only documented place Claude Code exposes it is the status line, the custom bar at the bottom of the terminal, so the design routes the number from there to the hooks.
short.hint: Tap a step to see what was checked and where it comes from.
items: The status line sees the percentage; hooks don't

The status line documentation (code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline) lists rate_limits.five_hour.used_percentage and rate_limits.seven_day.used_percentage, from 0 to 100, with a resets_at time. They arrive only for Pro and Max subscribers, and only after the session's first reply. The hooks documentation lists no usage field in any hook's input. A hook event called StopFailure fires with the matcher rate_limit, but only after the limit is already hit and the turn has ended, so it is too late for me to write anything.
Whether the desktop app runs a status line

The status line is documented for the terminal. The desktop documentation shows a usage ring next to the model picker but never mentions running a custom status line command, and I could not test it here: this cloud sandbox is not signed in to a Pro or Max plan, so it receives no usage data at all. The first build step is a one-minute probe on your machine that settles this.
Run one probe command in the desktop app and in the terminal, after the first step is built. I will hand it over as a step card.

The status line writes the two percentages to a small file. A hook reads that file after each tool call and at the end of each reply. At 90% it tells me to stop and hand off. If the limit is hit anyway, a StopFailure hook commits and pushes on its own, with no model call. A session-start hook on your other account finds the note and loads it.
Pick one answer for each question under Choices (detect, write and pickup), then send the approval line.
Send "Design approved: usage limit handoff" with your picks, for example "1A 2A 3A", or tell me what to change.

changes: keep
Commit and push rules (rules/detail/commit-branches.md)
The handoff commits under the existing rules, with no new permission.

Off main, I already commit and push without asking. On main, or on a branch that is yours rather than mine, the handoff first branches off to a new AjsAgent/handoff-<date> branch, which the rules already require.
keep
The handoff note shape (docs/handoff-2026-10-15.md)
The note reuses this file's sections: state, next steps in order, what was proved only partly, loose ends and where everything is.
That note was written by hand in an earlier session and is the format a fresh session already understood.
chg
Installer (tools/install.py)
It also sets the status line, wrapping any status line you already have.
The installer writes only the attribution, model and verbose settings.
It also writes a statusLine setting that runs the plugin's usage feed. If you already have a status line, the feed runs your command and prints its output unchanged, so your bar looks the same.

A plugin cannot ship a status line itself: Claude Code accepts only agent and subagentStatusLine from a plugin's settings.json (docs/3-state/ProjectState.md line 106). That is why the attribution setting goes through the installer too. --no-statusline skips it.
chg
New usage feed and warning (scripts/hook.py)
A new feed handler writes the percentages; the existing PostToolUse and Stop hooks read them.

At 90% of either window, the next tool call gets a notice telling me to finish the current step and hand off. The Stop hook then blocks my reply until a handoff note is committed and pushed. The threshold is HOUSE_RULES_HANDOFF_AT (default 90), and HOUSE_RULES_HANDOFF=off turns the feature off.
chg
New safety net (hooks/hooks.json, StopFailure)
If the limit is hit before the handoff, a hook commits and pushes the changed files and writes a short note on its own.

This note is mechanical: the branch, the changed files, your last message and my last reply, copied from the session transcript. It is worse than a note I write, but nothing is left uncommitted. It never runs on main.
chg
Pickup on the other account (scripts/hook.py, SessionStart)
A session that opens on a branch with an unfinished handoff note loads the note and says so first.
The note is marked done once the new session finishes its first step, so it is not loaded twice.
chg
Rule text, docs, tests and version
One sentence in rules/house-rules.md, a docs/4-systems/ page, verify.py cases and a version bump.

verify.py replays a status line input at 89% and 91% and a StopFailure event. The version is set at merge time: main is at 2.73.1, the background-tracking build takes a 2.73.x patch, and the unmerged restructure pull request takes 2.74.0, so this one is expected to be 2.75.0.
choices: detect
Where should the 90% reading come from?
A
The status line's documented usage fields
Documented and free. It works only where a status line runs: confirmed for the terminal, unverified for the desktop app until the probe runs.
B
The usage endpoint behind the /usage command, polled by a hook
Would work in the desktop app too, but the endpoint is undocumented, can change without notice, and needs the hook to read your sign-in token. I have not tested it.
C
No early warning; only the safety net when the limit is hit
Nothing new to install, but I never get the chance to write a proper note, so every handoff is the mechanical one.
Option A uses only documented fields. If the probe shows the desktop app runs no status line, I come back with option B as a separate proposal rather than building it unasked.
write
Who writes the handoff note at 90%?
A
I write it, and the safety net covers a hard stop
The note says what I was doing and why. Writing it costs part of the last 10%.
B
The hook writes it mechanically every time
Costs no usage, but the note is a file list and two messages, so the next session has to work out the rest.
The point is that your other account can pick the work up immediately, and only a note I write says what the next step is.
pickup
How should your other account find the work?
A
A note in docs/5-today/ on the pushed branch, loaded at session start
You open a session on that branch, and the note loads by itself. My last reply also gives you the exact line to paste.
B
Also post the note as a pull request comment
Readable from your phone without opening a session, but it adds a GitHub post to every handoff.
The note lives with the code it describes, and nothing goes outside the repo.

wrapup.summary: At 90% of either usage limit, I stop, write a handoff note, commit and push it, and your other account loads it when it opens the branch.
wrapup.changing: tools/install.py (status line), scripts/hook.py (feed, warning, pickup), hooks/hooks.json (StopFailure), rules/house-rules.md (one sentence), a docs/4-systems/ page, verify.py and the plugin version.
wrapup.blocking: Your approval and your three picks. Approving also creates one parent issue (replacing #140) and one issue per step before any code changes.
